title: Low-GI Frikadeller with Cucumber-Dill Salad
description: Traditional Danish Frikadeller use white flour and soaked white bread; replacing them with rolled oats introduces beta-glucan soluble fiber. The acetic acid in the cucumber salad actively blunts postprandial glucose absorption.
diabeticNotes: Traditional Danish Frikadeller use white flour and soaked white bread; replacing them with rolled oats introduces beta-glucan soluble fiber. The acetic acid in the cucumber salad actively blunts postprandial glucose absorption.

ingredients.name: lean minced pork or turkey (7–10% fat)
rolled oats (soaked in 2 tbsp water, replacing breadcrumbs)

steps.title: Mix Patty Base
steps.description: In a bowl, combine minced meat, soaked oats, egg white, minced onion, allspice, salt, and pepper. Mix with your hands until tacky and uniform. Shape into 3 oval patties.

steps.title: Quick-Pickle Cucumber
steps.description: In a separate bowl, toss shaved cucumber with apple cider vinegar, water, sweetener, fresh dill, and salt. Set aside to pickle lightly.

steps.title: Heat Pan
steps.description: Heat 1 teaspoon butter or oil in a skillet over medium heat.

steps.title: Pan-Sear Frikadeller
steps.description: Add meat patties and cook for 5–6 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through (internal temp 165°F / 74°C).

steps.title: Plate & Serve
steps.description: Serve hot frikadeller alongside the chilled, tangy cucumber-dill salad.
